title: Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (Increased Concessional Contributions Cap and Other Measures) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would temporarily increase superannuation contribution caps for older people, change low income contribution administration and reduce tax concessions for very high income earners.
It would introduce a $35,000 cap and apply additional tax rules where relevant income and concessionally taxed superannuation contributions together exceed $300,000.
The high income measures would apply from 2012-13, with special rules for defined benefits, certain State office holders and specified Commonwealth judges.
changes: The 2013-14 cap would rise to $35,000 for people aged at least 59 on 30 June 2013.
From 2014-15, the higher cap would cover people aged at least 49 on 30 June of the preceding financial year until the general cap catches up.
The Commissioner could estimate low income contribution eligibility after 12 months where information remains insufficient.
Low income contribution entitlements below $10 would be rounded up to $10.
Tax on defined benefit contributions would generally be deferred until a benefit is paid.
summary.affected: Older superannuation contributors, low and very high income earners, superannuation providers and the Commissioner of Taxation are affected.

speeches.speaker: Deb O'Neill
speeches.brief: Supported the superannuation bills, saying the $35,000 concessional cap will benefit 171,000 Australians over 60 from July and 363,000 aged over 50 from July 2014, and that the low-income superannuation contribution of up to $500 will help 3.6 million Australians earning under $37,000, including 2.1 million women.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: Criticised Labor's superannuation record, citing $192 billion in accumulated debt and a mining tax that collected only $200 million against a promised $3 billion, and detailed a 36 per cent increase in the self-managed super fund regulatory levy expected to raise $320 million over four years and affect more than 480,000 funds.
